description:
🌌 Team Legacy of Stars — Every Mission Leaves a Legacy!

We're passionate about space, technology, AI/ML, and storytelling. Our project, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” explores humanity's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars through interactive experiences powered by NASA data.
summary: Abandoned Silence is an interactive 3D field guide that helps young explorers discover machines humanity left on the Moon and Mars. Visitors choose a world, inspect glowing mission locations, and follow 17 child-friendly stories about landers, rovers, scientific instruments, and Ingenuity. Each story explains what the machine was built to do, what it discovered, where it remains, and why it never returned. A friendly guide, Pip, offers clues, read-aloud narration, short quizzes, collectible cards, and progress saved on the device. The project addresses the challenge by turning discarded space hardware into an accessible narrative about engineering, science, and the people behind exploration. Official NASA, JPL, and NSSDCA records support mission facts and link directly from the experience. By combining accurate sources with interactive storytelling, the project makes space history engaging for children, and classrooms.
details:
Abandoned Silence is a browser-based interactive field guide for school-age space enthusiasts. Visitors can choose the Moon or Mars, explore an interactive 3D world, and select mission locations. The experience contains 17 collectible story cards: seven Moon stories and ten Mars stories.

Each machine explains its history through four short sections: what it was, what happened during its mission, where it is now, and why it stayed behind. This framing helps users understand that equipment may remain in space because of engineering trade-offs, mission design, damage, power loss, or the absence of a return system.

Pip, an original astronaut guide, offers clues and optional read-aloud narration through browser speech synthesis. Every story includes a short knowledge check that awards a signal star. Users can save cards to a field journal, and their progress remains in local browser storage without requiring an account.

The intended impact is to make space history and planetary science easier for children, families, and classrooms to explore. The project combines emotional storytelling with transparent sources so that creativity does not come at the expense of scientific accuracy. We considered reading level, mobile usability, keyboard accessibility, reduced-motion support, performance, and the need to distinguish verified facts from creative narration.

We developed the project with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Framer Motion, Anime.js, CSS Modules, Lucide icons, the Web Speech API, and browser localStorage. Render hosts the live application, while GitHub hosts the public source code.

We transformed NASA NSSDCA mission catalog records and the challenge’s fourteen resource categories into a structured mission library containing launch dates, destinations, operational status, locations, instruments, discoveries, and end-of-mission information. This data powers the searchable resource library and linked stories rather than serving only as citations.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI tools assisted with coding and debugging. The team selected the concept, designed the experience, curated the stories, and checked mission claims against official NASA sources. No AI-generated imagery or video is included in the submitted experience or presentation. This independent project is not an official NASA website.
